title: Open-Source Essential Mathematics for the Victorian Curriculum Year 10 & 10A

chapters.title: Financial Mathematics, Surds, and Logarithms (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Compound interest, depreciation, inflation, operations with surds and rationalising denominators (10A), fractional indices and logarithms (10A).

sections.title: Compound Interest, Depreciation, and Financial Modelling
sections.vcaa_description: Recognise the effect of using approximations of real numbers in repeated calculations and compare the results when using exact representations; use mathematical modelling to solve financial problems involving compound interest (VC2M10A04).
sections.target_mastery: Apply the compound interest formula A = P(1 + r)^n across annual, quarterly, and monthly compounding periods, and model reducing-balance depreciation.
prerequisites: Simple interest and index laws (Year 9 VC2M9N02, VC2M9A01)
sub_concepts: Compound interest formula A = P(1 + r)^n
Non-annual compounding periods (monthly, quarterly)
Reducing-balance depreciation A = P(1 - r)^n and rounding error accumulation

sections.title: [10A] Operations with Surds and Rationalising the Denominator
sections.vcaa_description: Define rational and irrational numbers and perform operations with surds and fractional exponents.
sections.target_mastery: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide surds, expand binomial surd products, and rationalise monomial and conjugate binomial denominators.
prerequisites: Simplifying surds and DOTS (Year 9 VC2M9N01, VC2M9A02)
sub_concepts: Adding and subtracting like surds
Expanding binomials involving surds
Rationalising denominators including conjugate pairs

sections.title: [10A] Fractional Indices and Logarithms
sections.vcaa_description: Use the definition of a logarithm to establish and apply the laws of logarithms and investigate logarithmic scales in applied contexts.
sections.target_mastery: Evaluate fractional exponents a^(m/n) = (n-th root of a)^m, convert between index and logarithmic form log_a(y) = x, and simplify using logarithm laws.
prerequisites: Index laws with integer exponents (Year 9 VC2M9A01)
sub_concepts: Fractional exponents and n-th roots
Definition of a logarithm and log laws
Solving exponential equations and Richter/decibel logarithmic scales

chapters.title: Linear Inequalities, Simultaneous Equations, and Coordinate Geometry
chapters.description: Linear inequalities on the number line and Cartesian plane, simultaneous linear equations (substitution and elimination), and parallel and perpendicular lines.

sections.title: Solving Linear Inequalities and Half-Planes
sections.vcaa_description: Solve linear inequalities and simultaneous linear equations in 2 variables; interpret solutions graphically and apply to real-world contexts.
sections.target_mastery: Solve linear inequalities (reversing the inequality sign when multiplying/dividing by a negative), graph solution sets on a number line, and shade half-planes.
sub_concepts: Inequality properties and reversing the sign
Compound inequalities and number line intervals
Graphing linear inequalities in two variables

sections.title: Simultaneous Linear Equations: Substitution and Elimination
sections.vcaa_description: Solve linear inequalities and simultaneous linear equations in 2 variables; interpret solutions graphically and apply to real-world contexts.
sections.target_mastery: Solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations graphically, by substitution, and by elimination, and model break-even and mixture problems.
sub_concepts: Graphical intersection of two lines
Algebraic solution by substitution
Algebraic solution by elimination
Break-even analysis and applied linear systems

sections.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
sections.vcaa_description: Recognise the connection between algebraic and graphical representations of relations including parallel and perpendicular lines.
sections.target_mastery: Use m1 = m2 for parallel lines and m1 * m2 = -1 for perpendicular lines to find equations of straight lines and perpendicular bisectors.
prerequisites: Gradient, midpoint, and distance formulas (Year 9 VC2M9A03)
sub_concepts: Parallel lines have equal gradients (m1 = m2)
Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal gradients (m1 * m2 = -1)
Finding the equation of a perpendicular bisector

chapters.title: Quadratic Algebra and Equations (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Factorising monic and non-monic quadratics, completing the square, the Quadratic Formula, discriminant, and algebraic fractions.

sections.title: Factorising Quadratics and Completing the Square
sections.vcaa_description: Expand, factorise and simplify expressions and solve equations algebraically, applying exponent laws and algebraic fractions.
sections.target_mastery: Factorise monic and non-monic quadratic trinomials (grouping method) and complete the square to factorise over the real numbers.
sub_concepts: Completing the square x^2 + bx + c = (x + b/2)^2 - (b/2)^2 + c
Factorising non-monic quadratics ax^2 + bx + c by splitting the middle term
Simplifying algebraic fractions by factorising

sections.title: The Quadratic Formula and the Discriminant
sections.vcaa_description: Solve quadratic equations algebraically and graphically, and use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving quadratic functions (and 10A VC2M10AA02).
sections.target_mastery: Solve general quadratic equations ax^2 + bx + c = 0 using the Quadratic Formula and use the discriminant Delta = b^2 - 4ac to determine the nature of roots.
sub_concepts: Derivation and application of the Quadratic Formula
The discriminant Delta = b^2 - 4ac and number/nature of real roots
Quadratic modelling in geometry and kinematics

chapters.title: Parabolas, Exponentials, Polynomials, and Functions (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Sketching parabolas in all forms, exponential functions, circles and hyperbolas, polynomials (Remainder and Factor Theorems, 10A), and function notation (10A).

sections.title: Sketching Parabolas, Exponential Graphs, and Circles
sections.vcaa_description: Graph and investigate exponential, quadratic, circle and other non-linear relations, using digital tools and algorithms.
sections.target_mastery: Sketch parabolas in general, turning-point, and intercept forms, graph exponential relations y = a * b^x + k with asymptotes, and graph circles x^2 + y^2 = r^2.
sub_concepts: Finding turning points by completing the square or x = -b/(2a)
Exponential growth/decay graphs and horizontal asymptotes
Circles (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 and rectangular hyperbolas

sections.title: [10A] Polynomials, Remainder and Factor Theorems, and Functions
sections.vcaa_description: Investigate the concept of a polynomial and apply the factor and remainder theorems to solve problems; use function notation and inverse functions (VC2M10AA03).
sections.target_mastery: Divide polynomials, apply the Remainder and Factor Theorems to factorise and sketch cubic polynomials, and use function notation f(x) and domain/range.
sub_concepts: Polynomial long division and Remainder Theorem P(a)
Factor Theorem and solving cubic equations
Function notation f(x), domain, range, and inverse functions (VC2M10AA03)

chapters.title: Surface Area and Volume of Pyramids, Cones, and Spheres (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Surface area and volume of pyramids, cones, spheres, frustums, and composite 3D solids, plus logarithmic measurement scales.

sections.title: Surface Area and Volume of Pyramids, Cones, and Spheres
sections.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving the surface area and volume of composite objects using appropriate units (and 10A pyramids, cones, spheres VC2M10AM01).
sections.target_mastery: Calculate the total surface area and volume of right pyramids (V = 1/3 Ah), cones (TSA = pi*r^2 + pi*r*s, V = 1/3 pi*r^2*h), spheres (TSA = 4*pi*r^2, V = 4/3 pi*r^3), and composite solids.
prerequisites: Surface area and volume of prisms and cylinders (Year 9 VC2M9M02)
sub_concepts: Slant height vs perpendicular height in pyramids and cones
Surface area and volume of spheres and hemispheres
Composite 3D solids and logarithmic measurement scales (VC2M10M02)

chapters.title: Trigonometry, Bearings, and Non-Right-Angled Triangles (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: 3D trigonometry and true bearings, the Sine Rule, Cosine Rule, area of a triangle A = 1/2 ab sin C (10A), and the Unit Circle and trigonometric graphs (10A).

sections.title: Right-Angled Trigonometry in 2D/3D and True Bearings
sections.vcaa_description: Use Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry to solve spatial problems involving right-angled triangles in 2 and 3 dimensions.
sections.target_mastery: Solve multi-step navigation problems using three-figure true bearings (000 degrees T to 360 degrees T) and calculate angles and lengths in 3D space.
sub_concepts: Three-figure true bearings and back-bearings
Angles of elevation and depression in 3D solids
Multi-triangle trigonometric modelling

sections.title: [10A] The Sine Rule, Cosine Rule, and Triangle Area Formula
sections.vcaa_description: Establish and apply the sine, cosine and area rules for any triangle and solve related problems in 2 and 3 dimensions.
sections.target_mastery: Apply the Sine Rule (including the ambiguous case), the Cosine Rule, and A = 1/2 ab sin C to solve non-right-angled triangles.
sub_concepts: The Sine Rule a/sin A = b/sin B and the ambiguous case
The Cosine Rule c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab cos C
Area of any triangle A = 1/2 ab sin C

sections.title: [10A] The Unit Circle, Exact Values, and Trigonometric Graphs
sections.vcaa_description: Use the unit circle to define trigonometric functions as functions of a real variable, and graph them with and without digital tools.
sections.target_mastery: Determine exact values of sin, cos, and tan for angles in all four quadrants using reference angles (30, 45, 60 degrees), and sketch y = a sin(bx) and y = a cos(bx).
sub_concepts: Exact values for 30, 45, and 60 degrees
Unit circle definitions and CAST quadrant symmetry
Graphs, amplitude, and period of sine and cosine functions

chapters.title: Geometric Proofs, Circle Geometry, and Networks (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Deductive congruence and similarity proofs, planar graphs and network algorithms, and circle angle/chord/tangent theorems (10A).

sections.title: Deductive Geometric Proofs and Network Algorithms
sections.vcaa_description: Apply deductive reasoning to proofs involving shapes in the plane and use networks and network algorithms to solve spatial problems (VC2M10SP02).
sections.target_mastery: Write formal deductive proofs for triangle and quadrilateral properties and model spatial connectivity using weighted networks and shortest-path algorithms.
sub_concepts: Formal deductive proofs with geometric reasons
Vertices, edges, degree, and Eulerian/Hamiltonian paths in networks (VC2M10SP02)
Shortest-path and minimum spanning tree algorithms

sections.title: [10A] Circle Geometry: Angle, Chord, and Tangent Theorems
sections.vcaa_description: Prove and apply angle and chord properties of circles, and tangent and secant properties of circles (VC2M10ASP02).
sections.target_mastery: Prove and apply circle theorems including angle at the centre, angle in a semicircle, cyclic quadrilaterals, alternate segment theorem, and intersecting chords/secants.
sub_concepts: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
Angles in the same segment and cyclic quadrilaterals
Tangent-radius perpendicularity, alternate segment theorem, and secant power theorems

chapters.title: Conditional Probability and Independence (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Conditional probability Pr(A|B), independent vs mutually exclusive events, two- and three-stage experiments, and counting principles (10A).

sections.title: Conditional Probability and Independent Events
sections.vcaa_description: Use the language of 'if ... then', 'given', 'of', 'knowing that' to investigate conditional statements and identify common mistakes in interpreting such language (and VC2M10P02, VC2M10AP01).
sections.target_mastery: Calculate conditional probabilities Pr(A|B) = Pr(A intersect B)/Pr(B) from Venn diagrams, Karnaugh maps, and tree diagrams, and test for independence Pr(A intersect B) = Pr(A)Pr(B).
sub_concepts: Conditional probability formula Pr(A|B) = Pr(A intersect B)/Pr(B)
Testing whether two events are independent vs mutually exclusive
Counting principles, factorials, and sampling with/without replacement (10A VC2M10AP02)

chapters.title: Univariate Data: Box Plots, Quartiles, and Standard Deviation (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Five-number summaries, parallel box plots with outlier fences, cumulative frequency, and sample standard deviation (10A).

sections.title: Box Plots, Outlier Fences, and Comparing Distributions
sections.vcaa_description: Compare data distributions for continuous numerical variables using appropriate data displays including boxplots; discuss the shapes of these distributions in terms of symmetry, skewness and outliers (and VC2M10ST01).
sections.target_mastery: Construct parallel box plots, identify outliers using the lower fence Q1 - 1.5*IQR and upper fence Q3 + 1.5*IQR, and compare distributions.
sub_concepts: Five-number summary and box-and-whisker plots
Formal outlier fences: Q1 - 1.5*IQR and Q3 + 1.5*IQR
Calculating and interpreting mean and standard deviation s (10A VC2M10AST01)

chapters.title: Bivariate Data, Time Series, and Linear Regression (10 & 10A)
chapters.description: Scatterplots, lines of best fit, interpolation vs extrapolation, time-series trends, and least-squares regression and Pearson's r (10A).

sections.title: Scatterplots, Lines of Best Fit, and Time-Series Data
sections.vcaa_description: Construct scatterplots and comment on the association between the 2 numerical variables; fit a line of best fit and make predictions (including time series VC2M10ST04, VC2M10ST05, and 10A least-squares VC2M10AST02).
sections.target_mastery: Fit a linear model y = mx + c to bivariate data, distinguish between reliable interpolation and risky extrapolation, analyse time-series trends, and interpret Pearson's correlation coefficient r (10A).
sub_concepts: Fitting a line of best fit and interpreting gradient and y-intercept in context
Interpolation vs extrapolation
Time-series plots (secular trend, seasonality, cycles)
Least-squares regression line and correlation coefficient r (10A VC2M10AST02)
